official.description_text:
Postdoc in Sustainable Materials, Electrochemical Systems
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Engineering Sciences
Job description
The Department of Applied Physics is seeking a researcher in sustainable materials engineering, electrochemical technologies, and environmental process innovation. The position is placed in an internationally recognized research environment focused on developing advanced materials and processes for water purification, resource recovery, renewable energy conversion, and sustainable chemical production.
You will conduct research on functional nanomaterials and electrochemical systems for applications including capacitive deionization, advanced oxidation processes, photocatalysis, photo-Fenton water treatment, green hydrogen generation, and sustainable ammonia synthesis. The research will involve understanding charge transport, interfacial phenomena, catalytic mechanisms, and structure-property-performance relationships in nanostructured materials.
The work includes the design and optimization of materials and reactors using advanced characterization methods, data-driven approaches and AI-assisted workflows. Emphasis will be placed on accelerating the discovery of next-generation materials and processes that contribute to the transition toward a circular and sustainable society.
The duties also include supervising students and other researchers, collaborating with academic and industrial partners in Sweden and internationally, actively pursuing external research funding, and contributing to the scientific development of the group and department. Teaching and pedagogical activities may form part of the employment.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree in Materials Science, Applied Physics, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Nanotechnology, or related disciplines. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
Documented research expertise in sustainable materials, electrochemical systems, environmental technologies, photocatalysis, or renewable energy conversion demonstrated through publications in leading international journals.
Experience in developing advanced materials and nanostructures for water, energy, or environmental applications.
Excellent command of English, spoken and written, as the work is conducted in an international research environment.
As a person, you are creative, independent, and highly motivated, with excellent collaborative and interdisciplinary skills
Great emphasis will be placed on scientific excellence, innovation potential, and the ability to translate sustainable technology to industrial applications.
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
Demonstrated research experience in capacitive deionization, membrane-free desalination, water purification technologies, or resource recovery systems.
Experience with photocatalytic and photo-Fenton processes for environmental remediation and water treatment.
Research experience in electrocatalysis, green hydrogen production, carbon-neutral fuels, or sustainable ammonia synthesis.
Knowledge of charge-transfer mechanisms, interfacial electrochemistry, transport phenomena, and catalyst design.
Experience supervising doctoral students, master's students, or junior researchers.
Strong communication skills and demonstrated ability to translate research outcomes into societal and industrial impact.
Experience in leadership, project coordination, innovation activities, and industrial collaboration.
Awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Maximally two pages long.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).

The position offered is for, at the most, two years.

ai.summary: KTH postdoc position in sustainable materials and electrochemical systems (water purification, energy conversion, catalysis). Core focus is materials science, nanomaterials characterization, and electrochemical engineering with data-driven and AI-assisted workflows. Position emphasizes scientific excellence, industrial translation, and group leadership.

thematic_fit.rationale: No overlap with human-centred XR, immersive learning, spatial cognition, or collaborative systems. The posting is domain-specific materials engineering and environmental technology. Surface mention of 'AI-assisted workflows' does not create thematic connection to HCI or immersive systems research.

methodological_fit.rationale: Both researcher and position value experimental design and scientific rigor. However, the methodological contexts diverge fundamentally: the researcher conducts user studies, spatial transfer experiments, and HCI evaluation; the position requires materials characterization, electrochemistry, photocatalysis studies, and nanomaterial optimization. No methodological bridge exists.

growth_value.rationale: This position would not close capability gaps aligned with the target identity. The researcher would gain deep expertise in materials science and electrochemistry but would move away from human-centred research, immersive systems design, and spatial learning—core themes of the stated research identity. No synergy with long-term HCI/XR trajectory.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is a high-quality institution and Stockholm is in a preferred country (Sweden). However, strategic value is severely limited: the postdoc is in a different research domain, would not strengthen the researcher's position within human-centred XR communities, and would create a CV gap relative to the doctoral-researcher/PhD-candidate path in HCI. Position emphasizes materials innovation and industrial translation, not methodological or thematic alignment with target identity.

eligibility_flags: Requires PhD/equivalent by employment decision date; researcher holds MSc by Research in progress and would need to complete degree before eligibility.
Position classified as potentially security-sensitive under Swedish Protective Security Act; clearance may be required and could affect non-EU applicants depending on nationality.

Position explicitly targets researchers with 'documented research expertise in sustainable materials, electrochemical systems, or renewable energy' demonstrated via publications in leading journals—a domain outside the researcher's publication record.
risks: Critical domain mismatch: materials science/electrochemistry vs. human-centred XR. This is not a adjacent-methodological fit; the research contexts are orthogonal.
Career trajectory risk: accepting this postdoc would signal a shift away from the stated target identity and could reduce competitiveness for future HCI/XR doctoral positions.
Skill acquisition timeline: the researcher would require substantial ramp-up in materials characterization, electrochemistry, and nanomaterials knowledge with no prior background.

Publication misalignment: researcher's publication profile (orientation systems, immersive learning) is not competitive for this materials engineering role. New publications would take time to establish.
